---
title: "How could we more accurately model a throw?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 20.0
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0
PROBE_POOL = 120.0
PROBE_SPENT = 0.0

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import aerosandbox.numpy as np

opt_res = optimize_glider_3mm(verbose=False)
airplane = make_glider_3mm(
    c_root=opt_res["c_root"],
    taper=opt_res["taper"],
    cg_x=opt_res["cg_x"]
)
mass = opt_res["mass"]
Iyy = 1e-4

res = simulate_throw_3dof(
    airplane, mass, v_launch=5.0, pitch_launch_deg=5.0, 
    Iyy=Iyy, z0=-1.5, t_max=5.0
)

dist = res.y[0][-1]
t_flight = res.t[-1]
```

**Answer.** By modeling 3-DOF longitudinal rigid body dynamics instead of a point mass, we capture the pitch behavior of the glider (short-period and phugoid modes). The glider covers `{python} f"{dist:.1f}"` m in `{python} f"{t_flight:.2f}"` seconds. To keep the integration fast, we precompute a surrogate model of `AeroBuildup` forces across a grid of velocity, angle of attack, and pitch rate.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Specified
Asked of the user, 2026-09-18:

1. **Launch velocity: 5 m/s** — delegated to sensible human values.
2. **Launch pitch: 5°** — delegated to sensible human values.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Assumed
1. **Iyy: 1e-4 kg·m²**, unmodeled pitch inertia needed for 3DOF.
2. **Launch height: 1.5 m**, standard human shoulder height.
:::

```{python}
#| label: fig-throw-3dof
#| fig-cap: "Trajectory and pitch angle of a 5 m/s throw launched at a 5° pitch angle. Precomputing a surrogate model allows fast simulation of the rigid body dynamics."
fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(6, 6))
axs[0].plot(res.y[0], -res.y[1])
axs[0].set_ylabel("Height (m)")
axs[0].set_xlabel("Distance (m)")
axs[1].plot(res.t, np.degrees(res.y[4]))
axs[1].set_ylabel("Pitch Angle (°)")
axs[1].set_xlabel("Time (s)")
plt.tight_layout()
```
